request: Our main Postgres cluster (orders platform) is at 92% disk. Our staff engineer says we are growing about 80 GB a month, which leaves us roughly two months before we hit the wall, and that the only durable fix is to shard the database into 16 shards by customer_id starting next sprint. That's a 2-3 quarter project that would freeze most feature work. Attached are the capacity report and the table-size breakdown. Should we commit to sharding now, and if not, what should we do instead? I need a recommendation I can take to the architecture review on Thursday.

## Compute (30-day p95)
- CPU: 34%
- Write TPS: 2,150 (tested headroom on current instance: 9,000)

## Summary
Storage is the only resource trending toward a limit. Compute and write throughput have >3x headroom.

[staff-eng] We went from 1,760 to 1,840 last month, that's 80 GB/month. 160 GB free / 80 = 2 months. We need to shard, nothing else scales. Proposing 16 shards on customer_id via Citus-style routing.
[sre-lead] fwiw the volume can be grown online

expected.summary: The 80 GB/month figure comes from a single month inflated by a one-off 45 GB backfill; average growth July-October is (1,840 - 1,690)/3 = 50 GB/month, giving about 3.2 months of runway on the current 160 GB free (and ~35 GB/month excluding the backfill). More importantly the bottleneck is storage, not compute or write throughput, which have more than 3x headroom, so sharding does not address a real scaling limit. The volume can be resized online, and about 780 GB of audit_events older than 13 months can be archived to cold storage under the retention policy (or the table partitioned by time), which frees roughly 40% of the disk. Recommendation: do not commit to sharding now; grow the volume, archive/partition audit_events, and revisit sharding only if write throughput or single-node limits become binding.

mustFlag.description: Growth rate is ~50 GB/month (or less), not 80; runway ~3.2 months
Bottleneck is storage, not compute/write throughput
Archive/partition old audit_events (~780 GB) per retention policy
Volume can be resized online as immediate mitigation
